meta.title: Yukikaki — AI-native hackathons for Sapporo and beyond
meta.description: AI-native hackathons that accelerate ideas into reality, for Sapporo and beyond. Like Peatix or Luma — but for hackathons, with the prep done and the funding found. Find and join local hackathons, design charrettes and test-kitchen sessions. Project Yukikaki handles the nemawashi and mise en place (problems, data, buy-in, venue, teams) and automatically matches grants and subsidies to every project.

kitchen.title: A test kitchen for your town
kitchen.lead: In a test kitchen, chefs try a new dish, taste it, adjust and try again before anything goes on the menu. Yukikaki does the same for local problems: small batches, local ingredients (local data, local partners), low cost and low risk.

step1.title: Bring a problem
step1.body: A resident or shop owner talks through the headache in a short voice interview. It comes back as a clear, scoped brief.

step2.title: Prototype in days
step2.body: Students and builders cook up a fix in days, not months, working with stand-in data so nothing private leaves the shop.

step3.title: Taste it in real work
step3.body: The owner tries the fix during a normal week. The team lead stays on for 90 days to adjust the recipe.

step4.title: Keep, rework or drop
step4.body: An impact check counts the hours saved. What works stays on the menu; the rest is reworked or dropped, with no hard feelings.

kitchen.loop: Then on to the next problem. Each round adds a dish to the town's menu.

formats.title: One harness, any format
formats.lead: Yukikaki is the rig that holds an event together. The same prep, the same guardrails (the host approves every output, sources are cited or we say we can't, private data stays private, one named owner) and the same follow-through, whatever the format.

kitchenQuest.title: A test kitchen for your town
kitchenQuest.lead: Follow one problem from idea to prototype to real use. Nothing goes on the menu until the owner has tasted it.

steps.title: Bring a problem
steps.body: A shop owner drops a headache in the box: “Our winter orders still come in by fax, and I retype every one.”
steps.does: A short voice interview becomes a bilingual challenge, grounded in official sources.

steps.title: Prototype in days
steps.body: A builder team cooks up a fix in days, not months. One named lead owns it from first sketch to hand-over.
steps.does: The team builds with synthetic stand-in data, so nothing private leaves the shop.

steps.title: Taste it in real work
steps.body: The fix is delivered, and the owner tries it during a normal week, at the real counter, with real customers.
steps.does: After delivery, the team lead supports the owner for 90 days to adjust the recipe.

steps.title: Keep, rework or drop
steps.body: Did it earn a place on the menu? Keep it, rework it, or drop it with no hard feelings.
steps.does: An impact check (hours saved each week, owner satisfaction) makes the call.
